text:
Let

\[
I_n=\int_0^\infty x^n e^{-x}\,dx,\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots
\]

This is the Gamma function value \(\Gamma(n+1)\).

## Convergence

The integral converges for every non-negative integer \(n\): near \(x=0\), \(x^n e^{-x}\sim x^n\) is integrable, and as \(x\to\infty\), \(e^{-x}\) decays faster than any polynomial, so \(x^n e^{-x}\le C e^{-x/2}\) eventually.

## Base case

\[
I_0=\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx=\left[-e^{-x}\right]_0^\infty=1.
\]

## Recurrence by integration by parts

For \(n\ge 1\), take \(u=x^n\) and \(dv=e^{-x}dx\), so \(du=n x^{n-1}dx\) and \(v=-e^{-x}\). Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
I_n
&=\int_0^\infty x^n e^{-x}\,dx \\
&=\left[-x^n e^{-x}\right]_0^\infty+\int_0^\infty n x^{n-1}e^{-x}\,dx .
\end{aligned}
\]

The boundary term vanishes:

\[
\lim_{x\to\infty}x^n e^{-x}=0,\qquad \left.-x^n e^{-x}\right|_{x=0}=0 \quad (n\ge1).
\]

Hence

\[
I_n=n\int_0^\infty x^{n-1}e^{-x}\,dx=nI_{n-1}.
\]

## Induction

Since \(I_0=1\) and \(I_n=nI_{n-1}\), induction gives

\[
I_n=n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots 1\cdot I_0=n!.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{\int_0^\infty x^n e^{-x}\,dx=n!}
\qquad (n=0,1,2,\dots).
\]

In particular, for \(n=2\),

\[
\boxed{\int_0^\infty x^2 e^{-x}\,dx=2!=2.}
\]
